title: Regulatory Affairs Managers
description: Plan, direct, or coordinate production activities of an organization to ensure compliance with regulations and standard operating procedures.

tasks.text: Develop regulatory strategies and implementation plans for the preparation and submission of new products.
Review all regulatory agency submission materials to ensure timeliness, accuracy, comprehensiveness, or compliance with regulatory standards.
Direct the preparation and submission of regulatory agency applications, reports, or correspondence.
Investigate product complaints and prepare documentation and submissions to appropriate regulatory agencies as necessary.
Provide responses to regulatory agencies regarding product information or issues.
Represent organizations before domestic or international regulatory agencies on major policy matters or decisions regarding company products.
Provide regulatory guidance to departments or development project teams regarding design, development, evaluation, or marketing of products.
Manage activities such as audits, regulatory agency inspections, or product recalls.
Communicate regulatory information to multiple departments and ensure that information is interpreted correctly.
Maintain current knowledge of relevant regulations, including proposed and final rules.
Formulate or implement regulatory affairs policies and procedures to ensure that regulatory compliance is maintained or enhanced.
Direct documentation efforts to ensure compliance with domestic and international regulations and standards.
Review materials such as marketing literature or user manuals to ensure that regulatory agency requirements are met.
Participate in the development or implementation of clinical trial protocols.
Implement or monitor complaint processing systems to ensure effective and timely resolution of all complaint investigations.
Establish procedures or systems for publishing document submissions in hardcopy or electronic formats.
Establish regulatory priorities or budgets and allocate resources and workloads.
Train staff in regulatory policies or procedures.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures or local working practices.
Contribute to the development or implementation of business unit strategic and operating plans.
Monitor regulatory affairs activities to ensure their alignment with corporate sustainability or green initiatives.
Coordinate internal discoveries and depositions with legal department staff.
Monitor emerging trends regarding industry regulations to determine potential impacts on organizational processes.
Develop relationships with state or federal environmental regulatory agencies to learn about and analyze the potential impacts of proposed environmental policy regulations.
Monitor regulatory affairs trends related to environmental issues.
Evaluate regulatory affairs aspects that are specifically green, such as the use of toxic substances in packaging, carbon footprinting issues, or green policy implementation.
Evaluate new software publishing systems and confer with regulatory agencies concerning news or updates on electronic publishing of submissions.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Management of Personnel Resources
skills.def: Motivating, developing, and directing people as they work, identifying the best people for the job.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Electronic mail software
skills.def: Software to compose, send, or receive email. Examples: IBM Notes, Microsoft Outlook.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Document management software
skills.def: Software to store, organize, or search documents or files from other software or from paper copies. Examples: Adlib Express, Adobe Acrobat, Axway eSubmissions, Datafarm a-Pulse.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Database software, Microsoft Access, Structured query language SQL.
